chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, and others, from his father, from Khallad al-Qalansi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Makkah is the sanctuary of Allah, the sanctuary of His Messenger, and the sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). The prayer therein is equivalent to one hundred thousand prayers, and the Dirham (of charity) therein is equivalent to one hundred thousand Dirhams.

And Al-Madinah is the sanctuary of Allah, the sanctuary of His Messenger, and the sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). The prayer therein is equivalent to ten thousand prayers, and the Dirham (of charity) therein is equivalent to ten thousand Dirhams.

And Al-Kufa is the sanctuary of Allah, the sanctuary of His Messenger, and the sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). The prayer therein is equivalent to one thousand prayers, and the Dirham (of charity) therein is equivalent to one thousand Dirhams.

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمُ: Dirham (monetary unit used here for charity value)
key_terms.حَرَمُ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward multiplier for prayer and charity in Makkah, Medina, and Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the unique spiritual hierarchy of these three cities, explicitly linking the sanctity of Makkah and Al-Madinah to Imam Ali (AS) as 'Haram of the Commander of the Faithful,' a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of the Imams. The exponential multiplication of rewards (100,000x for Makkah, 10,000x for Al-Madinah, and 1,000x for Al-Kufa) reflects the Shia scholarly view that these locations are not merely geographical sites but extensions of divine presence and prophetic authority, with Al-Kufa serving as the political and spiritual center of the Imamate. This quantification emphasizes the merit of performing acts of worship in proximity to the Imams, reinforcing the theological importance of Al-Kufa as the fourth holiest city in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, and someone else, from his father, from Khallad Al Qalansy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

Makkah is a Harram of Allahazwj, and a Harram of Hisazwj Rasoolsaww, and a Harram of Amir Al-Momineenasws. The praying of Salaat therein is (equated) to a hundred thousand Salaats, and the Dirham (of charity) therein is (equated) to one hundred Dirhams.

And Al-Medina is a Harram of Allahazwj, and a Harram of Hisazwj Rasoolsaww, and a Harram of Amir Al-Momieenasws. The Salaat (prayed) therein is (equated) to ten thousand Salaats, and the Dirham (of charity) therein is (equated) to ten thousand Dirhams.

And Al-Kufa is a Harram of Allahazwj, and a Harram of Hisazwj Rasoolsaww, and a Harram of Amir Al-Momineenasws. The Salaat (prayed) therein is (equated) to a thousand Salaats, and the Dirham (of charity) therein is (equated) to a thousand Dirhams’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim and others have narrated from his father from Khalfad af-Qalanisiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Makkah is the sacred place of Allah, His messenger and ’Amir al-Mu’minin. Performing salat (prayer) therein is equal to performing one hundred thousand salat (prayer); giving one dirham charity is equal to one hundred thousand dirham charity.

Al-Madinah is the sacred place of Allah, His messenger and ’Amir al-Mu’minin. Performing salat (prayer) therein is equal to ten thousand salat (prayer) and giving one dirham charity is equal to ten thousand dirham.

Al-Kufa is the sacred place of Allah, His messenger and ’Amir al-Mu’minin. Performing salat (prayer) therein is equal to one thousand salat (prayer) and giving one dirham charity is equal to one thousand dirham.”
